title: Knicks sent employees fake offer of championship rings in phishing test: Report
gist: Madison Square Garden sent Knicks-organization staff a phishing-test email offering a free employee championship ring; employees who clicked had to attend mandatory cybersecurity training. MSG later called the lure "an unfortunate mistake", disclosed that it was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login obtained through a similar phishing attack, and said it is gifting more than 275 rings and jewelry worth over $3.7 million.

insights.claim: In late September the Knicks organization sent employees a phishing-test email saying their Employee Championship Ring was ready and asking them to click a link to choose between two designs, Championship Gold and Garden Classic.

insights.so_what: Shows how aggressive internal phishing lures have become.

insights.claim: Corporate phishing tests usually mimic company email but include telltale signs; Ars owner Condé Nast, for example, sends test messages from the misspelled domain condenest.com, and it is unknown whether the Knicks email had such tells.
